ignores_rate_changes.note: uses only the first rate in the schedule for the whole accrual period

ignores_grace_period.note: accrues interest starting the day after due_date, ignoring grace_period_days

always_actual_365.note: always divides by 365 regardless of the jurisdiction's day_count_convention

never_compounds.note: treats compounding as always simple, never capitalizes accrued interest

fee_threshold_off_by_one.note: triggers the late fee on due_date + threshold_days instead of + threshold_days + 1 -- a 1-day shift that rarely changes the outcome unless a payment or other event falls exactly between the two candidate trigger days, so this is the weakest probe measured; the pass bar is set specifically to still exclude it

allocation_principal_first.note: pays down principal before fees/interest regardless of the specified payment_allocation_order

rounds_daily.note: rounds each day's accrual to the cent instead of only the final total -- within the 5-cent tolerance (max observed drift 2 cents even over a 2-year accrual horizon), not a real bug worth penalizing

calibration.note: Each probe is a 'plausible but subtly wrong' implementation that gets exactly ONE rule interaction wrong while implementing everything else correctly -- not a strawman. The held-out scenario (266 queries: 15 hand-curated edge cases targeting specific rule interactions -- grace-period boundary, mid-window rate change, late-fee threshold boundary, fee-cap engagement, monthly compounding across February in both a leap and non-leap year, payment-allocation-order sensitivity, actual_365 vs actual_360, a long-horizon rounding-drift check, and a fee-triggers-before-grace-period-ends case -- plus 250 independently generated random cases) was scaled up from an initial 85-query version specifically to stabilize the weakest probe's measured percentage (it moved from 65.9% at 85 queries to a stable ~96% at 266, so the smaller sample was not a reliable read). The pass bar (262/266 = 98.5%) sits strictly between the weakest probe (256/266 = 96.2%) and the reference/tolerable-rounding-variant (266/266 = 100%) -- a narrower margin than the other probes show, but real: it survived a 3x scale-up of the held-out set without closing, unlike a probe whose apparent gap is just sampling noise. Unlike two earlier task designs this session (a subset-sum-style partition problem and a bipartite matching problem), this is a correctness task, not an optimization-quality task -- there is no heuristic that can partially satisfy multiple rules at once and land in between; each bug is caught deterministically by specific queries that exercise it. A genuine implementation bug was also caught and fixed during this calibration: the reference's own day-by-day loop started at accrual_start rather than at the earliest of accrual_start/fee_trigger_day/any payment date, silently skipping a late fee (or an early payment) that fell before interest started accruing -- fixed in reference_calc.py, solution/policy.py, and dev/plausible_wrong.py's shared base identically, and the fix's real-world impact (via payments landing before accrual_start with a 0-day grace period, not just the narrower threshold<grace scenario first suspected) is part of why the calibration numbers above differ from an earlier, smaller measurement.
